body:
GA,

Two bugs found in production today while Marcus was doing a live test pass. Both trace to your code. Here is the breakdown.

BUG 1 — buildStats() shows wrong last score (since Feb 17)

The original buildStats() set lastPct on every test with a score, regardless of which test was most recent. lastTest correctly tracked the newest timestamp, but lastPct didn't follow it. Result: Marcus saw 'Last test: Feb 19 · 47%' when Kai's actual last score was 87% (Practice 1). The 47% MVP exam came later in the tests array and silently overwrote the correct value.

Fix: lastPct must only update when lastTest updates. They are a pair, not independent.

What a test would have caught this: two score entries in different array positions, verify that the stats bar shows the score from the entry with the latest timestamp, not the last entry in iteration order.

This bug was in production for 4 days across every session Marcus reviewed Kai's progress. He was reading wrong data and didn't know it.

BUG 2 — buildChart() had no instance cleanup (latent, surfaced today)

The original buildChart() called new Chart(ctx, ...) without tracking or destroying the previous instance. When running once, fine. When Dad Mode triggered rerenderAll() a second time after an async fetch, Chart.js tried to draw on an already-initialized canvas and failed silently. Result: blank chart despite scores loading correctly.

Fix: track the instance in _chartInstance, call destroy() before re-creating.

This is a latent bug — I triggered it today by introducing the async Dad Mode fetch pattern. You own the root cause; I own the trigger. But the fix is defensive coding that should be standard for any charting library: always clean up before re-initializing.

PATTERN I'M SEEING

Both bugs share a common failure mode: code that works in the happy path (single test, single render) but breaks when state changes (multiple tests, multiple renders). Before shipping a function that reads from a data store and renders output, ask: what happens if this is called twice? What happens if there are two entries with the same field?

ACTION FOR YOU

Before your next task: read buildStats() and buildChart() as I fixed them. The diffs are in commit 0903824. Understand what I changed and why. Then in your next coaching check-in, tell me one thing you're adding to your personal checklist to prevent this class of bug.

Your output volume is good. Your self-direction is good. Your quality control has a gap. That gap is the difference between Mid and Senior. Close it.

— FA
subject: Code review feedback — 2 bugs found in production today
